Context: This excerpt is from a letter by Federalist Alexander Hamilton in which he discusses recommendations for the federal government.
Title: Source 3: [Adapted from] A Letter to Jonathan Dayton (1799)
Content: The measures that should be adopted are as follows:

— Efforts that will extend the influence and promote the popularity of the government. Under this are `text(three)` important actions. `text(First)`, the extension of the judiciary system. `text(Second)`, the improvement of roads. `text(Third)`, the creation of a program with funds to support new inventions, discoveries, and improvements.
— Efforts to improve the means and the strength of the government. Our navy should be completed with additional ships.

— Arrangements for confirming and enlarging the legal powers of the government. There are several laws that authorize the use of the militia to suppress insurrections. These laws ought to be permanent.
— A constitutional amendment for empowering Congress to open canals where they may be necessary to go through the territory of `text(two)` or more states.
— Laws for limiting and punishing seditious¹ practices. Doing so would uphold confidence in federal government officials by protecting their reputations from unfounded slanders.
References: seditious: persuading others people to revolt or oppose their government
